meta.title: Failure/Remediation Pipeline — Session Dashboard
meta.description: Say-again escalation ladder, qwen repair lane, and config-instantiated parser pipelines: what was measured, decided, and shipped

props.title: Say-Again Ladder, Qwen Repair & Pipeline Config
props.subtitle: One session: failure modes measured, escalation design decided, refactor executing

props.content: The ask: fail once → say again, fail twice → hand the turn to a qwen repair loop, all configurable. The finding: the candidate pipeline already IS the remediation framework — what's missing is turn-level state, and the worst failures (confident wrong parses) are invisible to any retry ladder.

props.label: Rows invisible to any retry ladder
Regex confidence — hardcoded, on every match
MEASURED
props.title: Three findings that reshape the design
props.subtitle: Each one was verified in code or measured against the fresh baseline — not assumed.

props.title: Confidence is a dead signal
props.content: The regex parser returns confidence 1.0 for any match. All 18 failing rows with readable confidence show exactly 1.0; the A1/A2 lane didn't serialize confidence at all (now fixed). A confidence-gated ladder catches zero of the 15 wrong-intent false positives.

props.title: The ladder only sees detected failures
props.content: Say-again escalation addresses at most 18 of 103 failing rows (no-parse + missing-slots). The ~31 confident-but-wrong rows never trigger it — they need a separate disagreement/validator lane that can veto or force-confirm, never bless.

props.title: Live say-again loops are unbounded
props.content: ConversationFSM (3-strike counter, spec'd and test-locked) is constructed only in tests. The live path is ad-hoc strings in the coordinator. Wiring the FSM is the prerequisite for any 'second failure' behavior — confirmed independently by two research passes.

props.label: FAILURE MODES
props.title: Where the 103 failing rows actually break
props.subtitle: Classified from the 2026-07-02 baseline. The class determines the remediation route — count alone is the wrong trigger.

props.label: EXPERT PANEL
props.title: Three critics, three verdicts
props.subtitle: Independent reviews grounded in the code maps, run before any design was fixed.

props.title: 🏗️ Architect
props.content: Your unification instinct is 80% right: repair output is just another Candidate through PolicyChain — never fork a second engine. What's genuinely new is the turn-level ladder. Single-shot rich-context qwen beats an agentic tool-loop: the 4B V27a is a structured parser, not a tool-caller, and injecting all evidence costs hundreds of tokens vs seconds per tool round-trip.

props.title: 🛡️ Safety / Authority
props.content: "Please standby" is controller→pilot phraseology — a pilot-side system saying it to ATC inverts the authority gradient. The #1 gap is stale-clearance turn-invalidation: a readback 15s late may confirm a re-issued clearance. Gate by intent criticality, not failure count; runway/takeoff/altitude never enter the LLM loop. Qwen tops out at advisory/confirm-only.

props.title: ⏳ Pre-mortem
props.content: The 3-strike ceiling is a hardcoded safety invariant — policy configures what happens within it, never the count. No free-form env × flight × aircraft config matrix: ship 3–4 named profiles, each with its own baseline row. Declare the numeric promotion metric before coding, or this repeats the grammar lane's months in shadow purgatory.

props.label: DECISION
props.title: FSM hosting: intent daemon, two phases
props.subtitle: /arch trade-off analysis across three candidates. Response daemon stays a stateless renderer; the coordinator string-path shrinks instead of growing.

props.title: Phase 1 — no new topics
props.content: Host ConversationFSM in the intent daemon, keyed per callsign beside the already-wired FlightStateTracker. Parse-side failures (no-parse, missing slots — exactly the ladder-visible classes) are all visible there today. Reconcile spec drift: max_clarification_attempts becomes a real constructor param, validated 1 ≤ n ≤ 3 — config can tighten the ceiling, never loosen it.

props.title: Phase 2 — close the loop
props.content: Add a response → intent turn-outcome feedback event so decision-gate and render failures also increment the counter. Ships only when the ladder needs those classes; the pending NATS-in-process config flag makes this hop nearly free later. Fitness functions lock the boundary: response may never import the FSM; attempts > 3 raises.

props.label: EXECUTION
props.title: What actually shipped this session
props.subtitle: Every slice is parity-gated: baseline-self-parity green plus row-for-row diff before acceptance. Workers' claims were replayed independently before being marked done.

items.title: Three code maps + three-critic panel
items.description: Say-again flow, candidate arbitration, qwen/config surfaces mapped with file:line evidence; architect, safety, and pre-mortem critiques synthesized into the options menu.

items.title: Failure taxonomy + confidence analysis
items.description: 103 failing rows classified into six classes; confidence proven a dead signal; the 31-row false-positive set is now a labeled eval asset (receipt in the workstream).

items.title: Two handoffs routed to other lanes
items.description: Qwen repair prototype (single-shot, shadow, advisory-only) for a parallel chat; 45 FMM-downstream rows routed to the FMM authority lane, merged with the existing regression-batch proposal.

items.title: Confidence serialized into A1/A2 baseline rows
items.description: observed_command_confidences on the FMM comparison, diagnostic-only. Parity green, display rows byte-identical, infra panel replayed by the controller.

items.title: Regression locks (codex worker)
items.description: Candidate-order and factory locks freeze today's behavior. Control experiment proved the 180 red tests in the full intent dir are pre-existing shared-tree drift.

items.title: candidate_source_order config key (codex worker)
items.description: Overlay YAML + fail-closed loader validation (raw-first, no duplicates, known names). Parsed but consumed by nothing; parity green.

items.title: Mechanical step extraction
items.description: The byte-identity risk slice: arbitration blocks become step functions, literal call order preserved. Gates: unmodified slice-1 lock, zero-row baseline diff, parity green.

items.title: Slice 4–5: config goes live, DeBERTa absence locked
items.description: Provider registry consumes the order list with startup fail-closed validation; DeBERTa's absence becomes a locked config fact. Then the repair pipeline is just a second overlay document.

props.label: YOUR CALLS
props.title: Decisions still open
props.subtitle: Everything else proceeds without input. These three change scope, so they wait for you.

props.title: 1 · Approve phase-1 FSM wiring
props.content: Intent daemon hosts the FSM, parse-side failures only, ceiling clamped at 3. Approval unlocks drafting the RemediationPolicy authority contract — the typed YAML that maps (count, criticality, failure class) → action.

props.title: 2 · Green-light the false-positive lane
props.content: Slice 1 is pure offline measurement: grammar-shadow disagreement + round-trip readback consistency scored against the 31-row labeled set, with the promotion bar pre-declared (recall at ≤1% false alarms on 1,152 passing rows).

props.title: 3 · failure_class as a baseline column
props.content: One deterministic function in the scorer emits the class per failing row — every future ratchet and the qwen prototype's repair-hit-rate become reportable per class. Cheapest when folded into the next scoring-script touch.
